module_title: The 3 Pillars of Measurement and the Circular Flow
introduction: Imagine a simple economy: A baker bakes bread (Production), pays his workers (Income), and the workers use that money to buy the bread (Expenditure). This is the 'Circular Flow of Income'. Because of this flow, National Income can be calculated at three different phases.

core_concepts.title: 1. Product / Value Added Method
core_concepts.description: This method measures National Income at the 'Production Phase'. It calculates the total value added by every producing enterprise in the country. (Value Added = Total value of output minus the cost of raw materials).

core_concepts.title: 2. Income Method
core_concepts.description: This method measures National Income at the 'Distribution Phase'. It calculates the total income earned by the 'factors of production' (Land, Labor, Capital, and Entrepreneurship) in the form of Rent, Wages, Interest, and Profit.

core_concepts.title: 3. Expenditure Method
core_concepts.description: This method measures National Income at the 'Disposition (Spending) Phase'. It calculates the total amount of money spent on final goods and services by households, businesses, and the government.

core_concepts.title: The Golden Rule of Equivalence
core_concepts.description: In a theoretical, error-free economy: Total Production = Total Income Earned = Total Expenditure Made. Measuring any of these three will give you the National Income.

important_entities.name: National Statistical Office (NSO)
important_entities.significance: In India, the task of calculating the GDP and National Income is entrusted to the National Statistical Office (NSO), which falls under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). *Note: The NSO was formed by merging the CSO (Central Statistics Office) and NSSO.*

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common beginner assumption is that the three methods give completely different numbers. Theoretically, they give the EXACT same number. Practically, there are slight discrepancies due to data collection errors, which statisticians adjust using 'Statistical Discrepancy' figures.

exam_strategy_tips: Always remember the nodal agency: The NSO (formerly CSO) is the singular authority responsible for releasing India's official GDP and National Income data.
